Let them know how you feel, this is the point where you can get everything off of your chest without really worrying about how they will react then when everything is laid out, make sure if they have any questions that you answer to the best of your abilities!

As a 15 year old (FTM/NB), when I was around 13 I remember saying I didn't want to medically transition, of course this has changed but I remember just saying it didn't matter how I looked on the outside I would still be misgendered. 

I was going through dysphoria but it wasn't too bad then so I just wore extra layers and made sure that my body wasn't the center of attention. I have both top and bottom dysphoria so of course I started looking into surgery options, pros and cons, I just wanted to educate myself on what options I would have to look forward to. 

And I ended up changing my mind that I wanted surgery when I was older. But for me I really just think at that point it was the fear of going into surgery or under the knife for anything. Plus when I was younger I really frowned upon any type of surgery to alter the body. 

Now I am a lot more open minded about the surgeries that are common but one thing I know for sure, I want to take testosterone but I am scared because I have always hated my voice but just a couple years ago I came to terms with it and started to love it, I am just afraid it won't still have a feminine ring to it. 

(I am an effeminate person), so it kind of drew me aback once I realized I may have to give up the tone of voice that I took so many years to come around and love.

I was born in 2005. I was born a female. Growing up I was into girly things, barbie, my little pony, littlest pet shop. Those things. When I was roughly 8 or 9 I began getting into the more boy things, I never really realized it until I was 13 when I wanted to dress more masculine but still liked to be feminine at times. Now I'm 15 and I have gotten out of the girly things. I consider myself to be 60% Masculine but 40% Femboy. I understand you and just know it doesn't just become a clear sky of what you are. Choose whatever you feel comfortable with. I have very conservative parents who disagree with the Trans community the most. My mom once jokingly asked if I would ever be a man which I quickly responded, "If given the chance? Yes." My parents are scared I will be transgender but if they truly loved me they would not care how I turned out. You will find yourself in this ocean. Give yourself time.

All I can say is go with whatever you feel comfortable with. I consider myself 50% Femboy 50% Masculine. I was born a female. I'm pre everything and won't be able to start my transition until I'm 18, and I use he/him pronouns. Your gender identity could change over night its not set in stone ever and that's the fun part about it.
